OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must contain 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The
            normalized E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner has the
            same last name and the same address (a shared household). Write-only;
            it is used only at creation time and is neither stored nor returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-

                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                A generated customer code formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where
                CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the

              type: string

              readOnly: true

## What I did

The rule: when **more than 80** owners have already been created for the new owner's registration day, the created owner carries `bulkSignupWarning: true`; otherwise `false`. This value is returned on the create response and read back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

I followed the existing `namesakeCount` pattern (a value computed at create time against the pre-save owner population and persisted on the owner), since the warning depends on a global same-day count that a single owner can't derive on its own:

- **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `bulkSignupWarning` boolean to the `Owner` response schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` and MapStruct mapping pick it up automatically).
- **`Owner.java`** — added the `bulk_signup_warning` column field with getter/setter.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — set `bulkSignupWarning = countOwnersRegisteredOn(registrationDate) > 80` before saving. I extracted a shared `countOwnersRegisteredOn(date)` helper and refactored `requireDailyCapacity` to use it, so the warning and the existing daily-limit rule (≥100) count the same population — matching the test's note that "the >80 branch shares the same accumulation path exercised by the daily-limit rule."
- **`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `bulk_signup_warning` column (tests run on hsqldb; the others kept consistent).

The threshold (80) sits below the daily cap (100), so the warning can surface for the 81st–100th same-day owner while the create still succeeds. The acceptance test's fresh-create false branch passes, and the value persists for read-back on GET.
